roadmap.title: The changes and their dependencies
roadmap.description: Solid arrows mean “depends on”. Click a node for its job, boundary and source. The two PRs contain implemented source; the amber F6 nodes are accepted design awaiting implementation.

nodes.label: Roles + practices
nodes.subtitle: Implemented source · reviewed
nodes.purpose: Seven responsibilities, Worker/Sidekick execution forms, progressive job packets, and one Verifier paired with each Implementer.
nodes.boundary: This is source-reviewed work. Draft PR status does not establish installed behavior or earned trust.

nodes.label: Five-document family
nodes.subtitle: Implemented source · reviewed
nodes.purpose: Requirements, Specification, Program Design, Test Design and Verification Design each own a different decision. Each has a local review, followed by integrated reading.
nodes.boundary: The family is stacked above #127. Its new design return exists, but current planners still consume the older three-document basis.

nodes.label: Main planner
nodes.subtitle: Spec accepted · not started
nodes.purpose: Plan Implementation reads all five documents and current closures, then schedules adopted test and verification strategy into slices, commands and prerequisites. It updates the canonical plan and actual consumers.
nodes.boundary: It does not choose a replacement oracle or test layer for an adopted design. Missing strategy returns to the design owner.

nodes.label: Improvement planner
nodes.subtitle: Spec accepted · not started
nodes.purpose: Plan Improve Repo adopts the same five-document basis for design-bearing findings and preserves positively source-proven mechanics-only work.
nodes.boundary: Audit-only exits, direct plan-only results, validation receipts and triage stay distinct. An incomplete design is never a mechanics-only fallback.

nodes.label: Structural proof
nodes.subtitle: Planned checks · not run
nodes.purpose: Permanent source-contract checks, existing schema tests, and a real source walk through producer → planner → handoff → executor/review. The paired Verifier reports finite observations.
nodes.boundary: String checks and schema parsing establish their structural claims; they do not show that a model follows the workflow.
nodes.source: F6 spec · Proof and independent review

nodes.label: Lead assessment
nodes.subtitle: Own reading and interpretation
nodes.purpose: The Lead opens the actual diff and decisive proof, checks them against the accepted need and design, and resolves every material gap before independent implementation review.
nodes.boundary: A helper report or a green count cannot replace the Lead’s understanding of what was required and observed.

nodes.label: Independent review
nodes.subtitle: Findings and correction closure
nodes.purpose: Independent reviewers inspect the implemented skills, their teaching, calls, claims and consumer consistency. The same review relationship checks bounded corrections.
nodes.boundary: Today’s accepted SPEC is not a review of an F6 implementation; none exists yet.

nodes.label: PR readiness
nodes.subtitle: Owner retains merge authority
nodes.purpose: Current PR head, checks, comments, review threads and mergeability are examined at the authorized delivery boundary.
nodes.boundary: This diagram starts no work, grants no merge, and claims no client refresh or runtime behavior.

design.title: What each design contributes to planning
design.description: This is the normal dependency path for an adopted substantial design unit. Every document has its own local review; the whole set has an integrated review. Early feasibility research can look ahead without changing who owns a decision.

nodes.label: Requirements
nodes.subtitle: Authorized outcome and boundary
nodes.purpose: The Lead clarifies the consumer, adopted outcome, constraints and scope with the owner. Requirements receives its local review and owner confirmation or explicit waiver.
nodes.boundary: No inferred preference becomes an authorized requirement.

nodes.label: Specification
nodes.subtitle: Entities, invariants and obligations
nodes.purpose: It defines what correct means through observable permitted and forbidden behavior, traced to Requirements, including domain identity and states.
nodes.boundary: It does not choose internal modules, persistence shapes, test layers or mechanisms.

nodes.label: Program Design
nodes.subtitle: Owners, interfaces and proof seams
nodes.purpose: It chooses responsibilities, interfaces, state, failure and concurrency realization. It names sufficient observation seams and what must stay real, with structural confirmation or waiver.
nodes.boundary: Test Design chooses scenarios and layers within these structural constraints.

nodes.label: Test Design
nodes.subtitle: Scenario → real interaction → oracle
nodes.purpose: It selects scenarios, independent oracles, the cheapest honest layers, substitutions, deterministic completion, and keep/repair/remove decisions.
nodes.boundary: A planned red is owed evidence. It is not an executed failing test. The Implementer writes product tests.

nodes.label: Verification Design
nodes.eyebrow: HOW the real system shows it
nodes.subtitle: Reference → route → observation
nodes.purpose: It names the independent correctness reference, real build/configuration/client, outcome observations, passing conditions, reuse and limits.
nodes.boundary: An acknowledgement, another target or a mocked path cannot prove the adopted outcome. Planned observations remain owed.

nodes.label: Integrated review
nodes.subtitle: Whole-set reading + final confirmation
nodes.purpose: After five current local review closures, an independent reader reconstructs the whole set. The owner confirms or waives the final set.
nodes.boundary: Five local verdicts cannot be relayed as the integrated reader’s judgment.

nodes.label: Ready design data
nodes.subtitle: Five documents + closures + owed proof
nodes.purpose: The cycle producer validates its own result. Planning receives its ready fields as data and opens the actual documents, confirmations and review evidence. Direct source-based planning verifies equivalent readiness.
nodes.boundary: The phase never imports an orchestrator-owned validator. Shared document/closure schemas constrain shape, not semantic correctness.

nodes.label: Planning
nodes.subtitle: Schedule it, preserve its meaning
nodes.purpose: Choose slices, concrete commands, dependencies, write scopes and earliest useful integration gates for the adopted strategy. Every owed test or observation is scheduled or returned as an exact gap.
nodes.boundary: No silent fallback to three documents; no replacing real proof with a cheaper check that cannot observe the claim.

nodes.label: Canonical plan
nodes.subtitle: Durable path + basis + delivery intent
nodes.purpose: One immutable Markdown plan links its current basis, proof obligations and intended delivery boundary. Handoff, implementation and review preserve the record.
nodes.boundary: A plan-only result stays non-executable. Tickets, handoff and validation do not upgrade authority or create another plan.
nodes.source: F6 spec · D5, D14 and D16

roles.title: Who owns the work and the judgment
roles.description: This view is role topology, not a dependency DAG. The dotted Implementer–Verifier link means shared facts and reproductions. Advice, observation, findings and acceptance are separate results.

nodes.label: You
nodes.subtitle: Meaning, tradeoffs and merge
nodes.purpose: You build the governing mental model with the Lead, settle owner-controlled choices, confirm adopted design decisions and retain merge authority.
nodes.boundary: You do not need to ferry routine logs or errors between helpers.

nodes.label: 🦉 Advisor
nodes.subtitle: Competing model and tradeoffs
nodes.purpose: Challenge the Lead’s assumptions and the inference from observation to claim. Bring a credible competing picture with source evidence, gains, costs and who pays.
nodes.boundary: Advice is not approval or independent review. It does not author governing design.

nodes.label: 🦁 Lead
nodes.subtitle: Design, plan, integration and acceptance
nodes.purpose: The owner’s main conversation. Writes the design and plan, cuts bounded assignments, reads decisive evidence, integrates results and accepts only claims it understands.
nodes.boundary: It cannot become a delegator who forwards “done.” A Verifier may run the observation; interpretation stays here.

nodes.label: 📚 Researcher / 🔧 Operator
nodes.subtitle: Checked answers / prescribed observations
nodes.purpose: The Researcher answers a supplied question from inspected evidence. The Operator scrapes, extracts, monitors or runs scripts under supplied criteria.
nodes.boundary: Neither owns architecture or acceptance. Cheap models do not acquire implementation authority. Worker/Sidekick describe how these roles run.

nodes.label: 🐒 Implementer
nodes.subtitle: Code + product tests + associated proof
nodes.purpose: Execute the Lead’s bounded plan, write feature code and product regression tests, run associated proof, and correct accepted implementation defects. Every Implementer has a paired Verifier.
nodes.boundary: Material design/plan meaning returns to the Lead. It does not author governing replacements.

nodes.label: 🔬 Verifier
nodes.subtitle: Outcome observation + test adequacy
nodes.purpose: Challenge proof feasibility early, check pyramid/TDD/sensitivity, inspect applicable real-path evidence and observe the adopted outcome. Own only assigned verification drivers/scripts.
nodes.boundary: No feature repairs or product-suite edits. Missing cases return to the Implementer; wrong expected meaning returns to the Lead. It does not accept delivery.

nodes.label: 🦁 Lead assessment
nodes.subtitle: Required outcome ↔ actual observation
nodes.purpose: Read the diff, the expected outcome and the actual target-bound observations. Determine whether the evidence establishes the claimed result and what remains open.
nodes.boundary: Verifier judgment is evidence to inspect. A receipt can be real yet test the wrong requirement.

nodes.label: 🔎 Reviewer
nodes.subtitle: Code, contracts, tests and corrections
nodes.purpose: Inspect ownership, types, state transitions, assertions and scope against governing sources. Detect tautological tests and assertions that invent restrictions. Verify corrected findings.
nodes.boundary: No editing or delivery acceptance. Review does not replace the Verifier’s real-system observation.
